A COM vtable method: an entry of the function-pointer table at 0x001CDDE0, whose entries are a run of distinct .text addresses stored by a constructor, so it is a function entry by definition. The translation pass read that table as a switch table, classified this address detection_method=tail_jump_alias and folded it into sub_000121D0 under the ff4d442 abutting-alias rule, deleting the body and pointing the dispatch tuple 0x000121B0 at sub_000121D0. A virtual call then enters the wrong function, and where the fold target calls the same slot again the guest self-recurses until the host stack overflows. Recovered so the address keeps its own body and its own dispatch entry. Body runs 0x000121B0..0x000121D0. Evidence: logs/runs/20260921-161002-066-vtable-class-recovered/ and the alias-fold findings in report-deepseek.md (2026-09-21).

A direct tail-jump target that no dword scan can find: sub_00074C70 ends at 0x00074CA9 with `jmp 0x6a770`, encoded `E9 C2 5A FF FF` (opcode 0xE9 + rel32 -42302 from 0x74CAE). The target is therefore a relative displacement, not a 32-bit literal, so the address 0x0006A770 occurs ZERO times in default.xbe -- confirmed by an exact dword search over the whole file, with the positive control that the same search finds 0x0013B750 and 0x0013FAD0. That is why every census and check-table-targets.py missed it: they enumerate stored dwords, and this target is never stored. Run 20261005-004233-759-f19-b0210 died on `[ICALL] Failed to resolve VA 0x0006A770` with the ICALL history naming 0x00074C70, after the 0x000B0210 fix landed. The analysis database has no entry in the gap: sub_0006A730 ends at 0x0006A769, six nop bytes follow, and the next entry is sub_0006A7C0. The body is a complete function: `push esi; push edi; mov esi,ecx; xor edi,edi; ...` looping `inc edi; cmp edi,5; jb 0x6a780` with the balanced exit `pop edi; pop esi; ret` at 0x0006A7B9, so stack_args 0. Boundary measured, not guessed: a linear capstone decode of 0x0006A770..0x0006A7C0 is clean with exactly ONE ret, at 0x0006A7B9, followed by a 6-byte nop pad to the next prologue 0x0006A7C0. This is the same unowned-gap class as 0x0013B750 and 0x0007AF90, but with a new detection blind spot: a relative-branch tail jump leaves no stored pointer at all.

The body really continues to the balanced epilogue `pop edi; pop esi; ret 4` at 0x0007DAD3, whose encoding is `C2 04 00`, so stack_args is 4 (the entry pushes esi then edi, matching the two pops). Boundary measured, not guessed: a clean linear capstone decode of 0x0007DA30..0x0007DAD6 has exactly ONE ret, at 0x0007DAD3, followed by nop padding to the next prologue 0x0007DAE0. This is the same class as 0x000B0210 -- an end tightened to a folded alias start -- with the additional finding that the truncated body hid a ret-immediate, so the wrapper delta was wrong as well. The previous value could never have been exercised, because the body had no ret to run.

The function 0x00118610 tail-calls this address and nothing covered it, so the guest trapped: [ICALL] Failed to resolve VA 0x001185B0 (run logs/runs/20260922-105928-501-apu-ack-spanfix). 0x00118610 is a recovered COM vtable method whose last instruction is `jmp 0x1185b0` at 0x00118622 -- a tail call *below* its own span start, which is why scripts/check-span-exits.py missed it: that check only looked for targets at or past `end`, so a backward tail call into a hole was invisible. The disassembler's own database missed it too: the body it knows before this one, 0x00118410, is recorded as ending 0x001185AA, six padding bytes short of 0x001185B0. A thread-startup trampoline the disassembler never claimed: it sits in a 439-byte hole between sub_0013B110 (ends 0x0013B179) and sub_0013B330, and no entry covered it. The title passes these addresses as ctx1 to PsCreateSystemThreadEx, and the thread wrapper 0x00147EBB calls ctx1, so the call failed with [ICALL] Failed to resolve VA 0x0013B180 in run logs/runs/20260922-085953-527-tailthunk-fix-ac97. Shape: spin on a per-thread flag word in 0x25EFA8-0x25EFDC counting iterations, run the worker loop, then push 0xF0000001, set the completion word and call 0x147E4E, which is the noreturn thread exit (push 0; call 0x147C6B; push [esp+4]; call dword ptr [0x1C4084]; int3), so the body has no ret of its own. Extent is the straight-line body up to and including the int3 that follows the exit call.

The analysis database has no entry at all here: sub_0013B610 ends at 0x0013B74A, a six-byte nop pad follows, and the next entry is sub_0013B810 -- a 198-byte unowned gap. The body is a complete function: `push ebp; push esi; mov esi,[esp+0xc]; ...` with two `ret` exits at 0x0013B7EE and 0x0013B808, balanced by pop edi/esi/ebp, so stack_args 0. End is the next prologue, 0x0013B810, matching the 0x0013FAD0 convention (trailing nop pad included). A render-scene vtable slot with its own original body. The render-scene vtable at 0x001E0F00 holds 0x0014FEF0 at slot +0x148, the dword at 0x001E1048, between 0x0014FDE0 at +0x144 and 0x0014FE30 at +0x14C; the per-frame scene-state calls at 0x0013DDC and 0x0013F03 are `call dword ptr [edx+0x148]`. Seven neighbouring slots of that same table are already reviewed recovery entries -- 0x0014FDE0, 0x0014FE30, 0x0014FE50, 0x0014FE60, 0x00150130, 0x00150170 and 0x001501F0 -- so the address is a function entry by its own bytes and by that context, not by an assumption about the whole table. The analysis database classifies it detection_method=tail_jump_alias with inferred end 0x00150231, and the generated dispatch folded the address onto the alias wrapper: recomp_dispatch.c holds both the alias map pair { 0x0014FEF0u, 0x00150231u } and the tuple { 0x0014FEF0u, (recomp_func_t)recomp_alias_0014FEF0 }, and the archived run records the substitution itself as `[ALIAS-ICALL] target=0x0014FEF0 owner=0x00150231` at logs/runs/20261002-132843-938-owner-d2-kernel-noop-600/jsrf_run.log:2652. The alias owner is not this function: 0x00150231 is only the shared E_INVALIDARG tail of the neighbouring 0x001501F0 (`mov eax,0x80070057; ret 0xC` at 0x00150231), so the fold drops the real body while keeping the stack balanced. Own original bytes establish the span instead of the database's inferred end 0x00150231, which crosses other real functions: the body is [0x0014FEF0,0x00150104) -- `mov eax,[esp+8]` / `mov edx,[esp+0xC]` / `xor ecx,ecx` / `test eax,eax` / `setne cl` / `cmp edx,9` at 0x0014FEFF / `ja 0x150075` at 0x0014FF03 / `jmp dword ptr [edx*4+0x150104]` at 0x0014FF09. The pointer-argument path at 0x00150075 reads a stage record through edx and writes 0x19DF10/18/1C/20/28/2C; the ten switch cases write the per-stage texture/combiner state at 0x19DF10..0x19DF2C + (stage<<7) and set the dirty flags at 0x19DED8 (0x800, plus 0x480F on the pointer path), then return S_OK. Every path ends in `ret 0xC`, so the callee cleans 12 argument bytes and the recovery wrapper checks ESP+16; the function makes no calls and contains no loops. Its own jump table is [0x00150104,0x0015012C), ten dwords: 0014FF10 0014FF3C 0014FF68 0014FF72 0014FF81 0014FF8B 0014FFC3 0014FFD5 0015001A 0015002C -- all ten lie inside the body, so the span stops at 0x00150104 and excludes the table data, as with the reviewed switch recoveries 0x00026780 and 0x00037550; four NOPs then precede the next function entry at 0x00150130. This is a byte- and table-backed restoration of a real render-state method, not a title or fade causal fix: the two sampled callers do not branch on the returned HRESULT, so no fade-done or SEGA-departure claim follows from it. Evidence: docs/reviews/owner-sega-600-observations.md, section 'Own-byte / table evidence and proposed L02 repair' (2026-10-02).

A virtual call then enters the wrong function, and where the fold target calls the same slot again the guest self-recurses until the host stack overflows. Recovered so the address keeps its own body and its own dispatch entry. Body runs 0x00158D70..0x00158DF0. Evidence: logs/runs/20260921-161002-066-vtable-class-recovered/ and the alias-fold findings in report-deepseek.md (2026-09-21).

A real function the disassembler never claimed, in a hole between sub_00178E70/sub_00178E85 (both end 0x00178F34) and 0x001791C0. The title calls it indirectly and the call failed with [ICALL] Failed to resolve VA 0x00178F40 in run logs/runs/20260922-090256-907-trampoline-fix, immediately before the 0xE0424943 exception -- so that exception is a symptom of this unresolved call, not a separate defect. Shape: normal prologue sub esp,0x14; push ebx; mov ebx,[esp+0x1C]; mov eax,[ebx+0xC]; push ebp; xor ebp,ebp; cmp eax,-1; push esi; push edi. It reads five stack arguments: arg1 at [esp+0x1C] right after the frame and the one push, then arg2 [esp+0x2C], arg3 [esp+0x30], arg4 [esp+0x34] and a byte arg5 at [esp+0x38] once all four registers are pushed. Epilogue measured: 0x001791A3 mov ecx,[esp+0x34]; test ecx,ecx; pop edi; pop esi; pop ebp; pop ebx; 0x001791B5 add esp,0x14; 0x001791B8 ret 0x14. The ret 0x14 matches the sub esp,0x14 prologue, so stack_args is 20. It returns E_INVALIDARG (0x80070057) and CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED (0x800401F0). END CORRECTED to 0x001791BB: end is exclusive and the original value 0x001791BA cut the last byte of the three-byte `ret 0x14` (C2 14 00 at 0x001791B8..0x001791BA), so the translator could not decode the return at all, emitted a body with no epilogue and no return statement, and the run aborted with `[RECOVERED] ABI FAILURE 0x00178F40 esp 00F7FDA0->00F7FDA0 expected +24` in logs/runs/20260922-101516-467-p1-178f40. Measured with scripts/inspect-jsrf.py data 0x001791B4 8 -> 1183C414 900014C2, i.e. bytes 11 83 C4 14 | C2 14 00 90. Evidence: report-deepseek.md, 2026-09-22.

A C++ static initializer, and the first real guest failure after guest_entry. The initializer array runs from 0x001EB760 to 0x001EB76C; the walker 0x0014B50D calls every non-null, non-(-1) dword in that range, and slot 0x001EB764 holds 0x0017E58F. The body is self-contained and does not fall through into 0x0017E600: it calls 0x0017F1D7, tests EAX, allocates 0x84 bytes through 0x00180D39, stores the object pointer via fs:[4]/[0x264850], writes the vtable 0x0022F198 at +0x54 and 1 at +0x14, calls 0x00147FA7 and 0x00147E72, and returns through the plain ret at 0x0017E5F4. int3 padding fills 0x0017E5F5..0x0017E600. The translation pass classifies this address detection_method=tail_jump_alias and folds it into the next entry 0x0017E600, which deletes this body and points the dispatch tuple 0x0017E58F at sub_0017E600. 0x0017E600 is the three-argument catch-frame invoker, so it reads its handler/context/flags from its caller's stack; the zero-argument initializer call therefore reads [ebp+8]=0x00700010 and dies on call eax at 0x0017E625. Recovered here so the address keeps its own body and its own dispatch entry. kind=routine, not the initializer default, because this body calls other framed functions (0x00180D39, 0x00147FA7, 0x00147E72) and a generated epilogue emits POP32(esp, ebp) without restoring g_ebp, so g_ebp is a last-published-frame hint and is expected to drift across calls. Measured with the initializer check enabled: esp 0x00F7FF44->0x00F7FF48 (expected +4), ebx/esi/edi preserved, g_ebp 0x00F7FF0C->0x00F7FF1C. Guest EBP is preserved by construction - the body never assigns ebp. Evidence: logs/runs/20260921-154535-674-resume-check/ (stacks.txt guest registers esi=0x001EB764 edi=0x001EB76C, which are the walker's own loop pointers).

The actual submit path. RET 4 (0x00190332) so it takes one argument, a mode/flags dword. It is the only route from a method block to the GPU. ARG 0x00190240: reads the argument at 0x00190240, tests bit 4, and sets bit 9 of the flags word context+0x08 when the bit is present or clears it otherwise, storing the argument with bit 4 masked off into context+0x2018. ARG 0x0019025A-0x0019026C/NZ (0x19026C jne) takes a short path that ORs 0x1600 into the global at 0x0019DED8 and then locks the pushbuffer. It guards the cursor against the commit limit through 0x001916B0, writes a 0x30-dword (0xC0-byte) record at the cursor starting with 0x41EA4/0x3C/0x300B80, copies 12 dwords from the constant table at 0x0019A228 into the record, then lays down four 0x44-byte per-surface blocks built by 0x00190FB0 with source rule 0x0019A170 and targets 0x4008 40/80/C0/900. It terminates the record with the float constant 0x1009D0, two zero dwords, 1.0f at +0x11 8 and a zero, advances the write cursor by 0x124 bytes, and returns. Reached from 0x001918CB (inside 0x001917F0) with a zero argument and from other publish paths.

Submission-record field copier called three times by 0x00190240 (0x001902BB, 0x001902CE, 0x001902E4, 0x001902FA) with three cdecl arguments: destination, destination-dword-index, and a 0x40-byte source record at 0x0019A170/0x0019A228. Re-lays the 16 sampled source dwords (offsets 0x00,0x10,0x20,0x30,0x04,0x14,...,0x3C) into 17 consecutive destination dwords, so destination+0x44 is exactly where the next call's destination starts. Ends RET 0xC at 0x0019101D; NOP padding runs 0x0019101D-0x0019101F.
Direct CALL at 0x00192112 with ECX=device. Allocates pushbuffer and bookkeeping from configured sizes, bounded shift loop, restores ESI and RET at 0x001910B6.

Ring teardown. Thiscall ECX=ring context, no stack arguments (plain RET at 0x001910DF). Frees the mapped region context+0x24 through the imported releaser at 0x001C404C when non-null, then frees the submission record table context+0x4C through 0x0014A85B when non-null. This entry owns only the 10 instructions at 0x001910C0-0x001910DF; the code at 0x001910E0 is a separate function that is reached by fall-through from 0x001910DF, so it must be registered as its own entry.

Ring byte-accounting helper. Entered only by fall-through from 0x001910DF, never by CALL, so it is an internal entry that the lifter must still treat as a callable boundary because the preceding function RETs before it. ECX=ring context, EDX=submission record pointer, no stack arguments (plain RET at 0x0019112F and 0x00191140). Computes, modulo the wrap byte count context+0x44, the submitted dword distance between the record's start and end pointers, clamping negative results to zero, then adds the record's queue-depth field at record+0x08 minus context+0x2AB8. Returns the clamped total in EAX. Reached from 0x00191480/0x001914C1 inside the back-pressure wait.

Submission lookup/rotate. Custom convention: EAX carries the target ring position and one dword is read from [ESP+0x14] (the caller's first stack argument) at 0x0019116D; no RET immediate (plain RET at 0x001911C7, 0x00191256, 0x00191260), so the argument is read but never popped. Called by 0x00191473 with EAX=guest position and by 0x00191xxx publish paths. When the write cursor context+0x30 is within 0x80 dwords of the requested position it walks the submission record array context+0x4C with mask context+0x3C, comparing wrapped record start positions against the current cursor, and returns the matching record pointer in EAX or zero when the ring wraps past the queue head. Returns zero (0x00191257) when no record matches. All six exits restore EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI and leave the stack unchanged.

The kick primitive itself. No arguments at all (no prologue, plain RET at 0x0019129C). Loads the ring context from MEM32[0x0019DCE0], follows context+0x2268 to the mapped NV2A register base, issues SFENCE, then reads-modifies-writes NV_PFB_WBC (register base + 0x100410) with NV_PFB_WBC_FLUSH (bit 16) set, and spins at 0x00191290 until the flush reads back idle. An earlier reading called this register NV_PFIFO_CACHE1_DMA_PUT; see the correction in docs/jsrf-kick-get-contract.md. Called from 0x001914B8 and 0x001914DB inside the back-pressure wait. It is never called from the 0x001918E0/0x001917F0 method blocks; those publish through 0x00190240.

Framebuffer publish helper called by 0x00192090 after WBINVD. Thiscall ECX=D3D device, RET 0. When device+8 bit 0x2000 is clear it SFENCE-flushes NV_PFB_WBC at [*0x19DCE0+0x2268]+0x100410, then stores the masked primary address. When 0x19DED0 is zero it skips unresolved 0x0018E120. The 0x2000 path publishes 0x19DE88 into device+0x2264 without touching WBC. Keep 0x0018E120 fatal.

Submission record path. Stdcall one argument (RET 4 at 0x0019143A) selecting the record mode. Reads the ring context from MEM32[0x0019DCE0] rather than ECX. If the write cursor has reached the commit limit it first reserves space through 0x00191530 with (MEM32[0x0019E328], MEM32[0x0019E328]>>1). Emits a two-dword command pair at the cursor carrying the kernel read pointer context+0x30, then advances context+0x30 by two dwords and records the new cursor in the submission slot selected by (context+0x30>>1)&0x3F at context+0x50 + slot*12, storing the pointer at +0x50 and the published context+0x40 value at +0x58. When the argument has bit 0 set it also advances the submission counter context+0x38 under mask context+0x3C and writes the three-dword record {read pointer, record, published PUT} into the table at context+0x4C. When bit 1 is clear it calls the kick path 0x001912A0; when bit 1 is set it returns without kicking. Returns the pre-update read pointer in EAX.

Back-pressure wait. RET 8 at 0x001914FE and 0x00191523 (one explicit add esp,8 before 0x0019144C's sibling) so it takes two dwords; the first is read as the target ring position at 0x00191441. Reads the GPU-side GET from [context+0x34] and compares it against the kernel write pointer context+0x30; when the ring is not already exhausted it loops over the submission records, and if the requested record has been retired it returns immediately (0x0019145E -> 0x001914FC). Otherwise it calls 0x00191150 to find the record, accounts its bytes through 0x001910E0, and when the accounted size reaches 0x8000 dwords it programs a 0x40110/0x40100 register pair into the record and kicks twice through 0x00191270. When the accounted size is still at or above 0x8000 on the second check it releases an OS wait object: it pushes the 1C4018 import target and calls through EDI with (1, 6, 1, 0, 0) until the call returns zero (0x00191510-0x0019151D), then returns. The final loop at 0x001914F0 re-reads GET until the write cursor distance is covered.

The GET wait and ring reservation. RET 8 (0x00191666 and 0x001916A0) so it takes two dwords. Fast path: when bit 2 of the flags word context+0x08 is set it advances the kernel write pointer by the head record's start at [context+0x350]+4, adds the write-cursor delta into context+0x354, sets the write cursor to the head record's start, and returns that value in EAX (0x00191543-0x00191566) without touching the GPU. Otherwise it computes the reservation size as the requested size plus one dword, derives the effective ring position from context+0x2264's mapped descriptor at +0x44 ORed with 0x80000000 and clamped into [context+0x24, context+0x28) or taken from context+0x438+0x324C, folds the wrap byte count context+0x44, writes the next-submission marker into the cursor, and when the request crosses the ring end it rotates the cursor back to context+0x24 and publishes the remnant. It then scans the submission table context+0x4C for a record whose span covers the reservation and calls 0x00191440 with (record, 1) to retire it. Finally it stores the new commit limit context+0x04, and if bit 12 of the flags word is set it ORs 0x1000 into context+0x08 and calls the publish/kick path 0x001912A0, else it calls 0x00191390 with mode 1 first and then 0x001912A0. Returns the write cursor in EAX. This is the function that finally reaches the kick latch on the live boot path.

Ring wrap adjuster. No arguments (plain RET at 0x001916BE). Pushes MEM32[0x0019E328] and MEM32[0x0019E328]>>1 and calls the reservation path 0x00191530, so it is simply 0x00191530(ring_size, ring_size/2) with the frame's stack balanced by the callee's RET 8. Called from 0x001918F0, 0x001917FF, 0x0019186B and 0x00190283 immediately before a record is written at the cursor, which is why every one of those sites is guarded by 'cmp cursor, limit / jb skip'.

Bounded reserve. RET 8 (0x00191705 and the fall-through into 0x00191530) so it takes two dwords: a pointer to a {cursor, limit} pair at [ESP+4] and a dword count at [ESP+8]. When cursor + count*4 is below limit+0x200 it returns immediately without reserving. Otherwise it raises the limit to max(limit, (count*4 + 0x204)/2) and re-enters 0x00191530 through the tail jmp at 0x00191700 with the adjusted pair, so the reserve is retried against the widened ring. No caller sites were found in the 0x0019xxxx region; it is an internal helper of the ring codec.

Poll-current helper. No arguments (plain RET at 0x00191720). Reads the ring context from MEM32[0x0019DCE0], takes the kernel write pointer context+0x30 and calls the back-pressure wait 0x00191440 with (pointer, 0). No caller sites were found; it is the 'wait for everything queued so far' entry point of the ring codec.

Submission retire helper. RET 4 at 0x00191771, 0x00191795 and 0x001917A5, so one argument: a record pointer. Returns immediately when MEM32[0x0019DCE0] is null. Masks the record's flags dword with 0x70000 and, when the result is 0x50000 and record+0x14 is non-null, calls 0x001928D0 with the record and, if it fails, waits on the current kernel write pointer through 0x00191440. Otherwise it waits on record+0x08 first, and when that too fails and the returned value at 0x00191774 is non-zero it waits on that value. Every exit returns the record pointer in EAX after the wait, which is how callers learn the final position.

Second-record retire helper. RET 4 at 0x001917D4 and 0x001917E3, so one argument: a record pointer. Returns immediately when MEM32[0x0019DCE0] is null. When any of bits 19-22 of the record flags dword are set it waits on the current kernel write pointer through 0x00191440; otherwise it waits only when record+0x08 is non-zero. This is the sibling of 0x00191730 for records whose flags do not carry the 0x50000 class tag.

Second pushbuffer method block. No arguments and no stack cleanup (plain RET at 0x001918D2). Reads the ring context from MEM32[0x0019DCE0], guards the cursor against the commit limit through 0x001916B0, then writes a 0x3C-byte (15-dword) method record at the cursor carrying NV2A methods 0xC0180/2, 0x3 and 0x3 header dwords, 0x180190/4, 9, 0xA, 0x3, 0x3, 8, 0x401A8/0xC, 0x41D6C and a zero terminator, advances the write cursor by 15 dwords, re-checks the limit through 0x001916B0, writes a second 15-dword record carrying 0x409FC/1, 0x100A50, three zero dwords, the float 1.0f at +0x18, 0x416BC, 1, 0x41E78, 0x210000, 0x41D80, 1, 0x41E68 and the float +inf at +0x38, advances the cursor again, and finally emits the block by pushing a zero argument and calling the submit path 0x00190240. Reached by the tail jmp at 0x001919B9 from 0x001918E0, which is why the preceding block has no RET of its own.

The first pushbuffer method block and the current boot stop. No arguments and no stack cleanup; it ends by tail-jumping to 0x001917F0 at 0x001919B9 instead of returning, so 0x001917F0 inherits its frame (EBX/ESI/EDI are pushed at 0x001918E0/0x001918E1/0x001918ED and only 0x001917F0's epilogue pops them). Saves EBX/ESI/EDI, reads the ring context from MEM32[0x0019DCE0], guards the cursor against the commit limit through 0x001916B0, then writes an 11-dword method record at the cursor: 0x42000/0xE, 0x44000/0x10, 0x46000/0x11, 0x40000/0xD, 0x42180/7 and 0x442FC/3, where the leading NV2A method IDs are 0x042000, 0x044000, 0x046000, 0x040000, 0x042180 and 0x0442FC. Advances the write cursor by 11 dwords, clears the 16-dword blocks at context+0x201C and context+0x203C with rep stosd, and writes the 15-dword pair-tag record 0x31C4184... starting with 0x86184/3/0xB at context+0x2030 through context+0x2040 and then eight 0x19 dwords, terminating with 0x11. This is the method block the live boot reaches, so recovering it is what turns the fatal unresolved-call into a real submission.

Direct CALL 0x0018E4C4, ECX points to guest device at 0x0019B200, one guest presentation-parameters pointer on stack. Original internal branches bounded to final RET 4 at 0x0019259D; includes GPU resource/queue initialization and fence wait at 0x00192460.
Direct CALL 0x001999AD in recovered enumeration path. Converts mode bits to display flags, final RET 4 at 0x001935BD.
Direct CALL from distinct next routine at 0x001935E5; cached display setting query, RET at 0x001935DE.
Direct calls from 0x0019983F/0x001998EB; separate prologue after preceding RET, all forward/backward branches bounded and final RET at 0x00193657. Selects video mode table entry from 0x0019A728.

Self-contained timestamp leaf confirmed by original disassembly as RDTSC at 0x00193C40 followed by RET at 0x00193C42. Uses the established runtime Xbox-scaled timestamp primitive, returning EDX:EAX exactly as the x86 instruction and preserving all other guest state.

Exact queue submission helper confirmed by original disassembly. ECX=context, [esp+4]=payload passed to unresolved 0x0018E500, and [esp+8]=stored at context+0x210. Selects slot=(context+0x1F0)&1; when context+0x814+slot*4 equals 1, calls unresolved 0x0018E584(context, context+0x214+slot*0x300), then clears that status. Sets device+0x40071C bit 1, increments the context index with x86 wrap, copies context+0x1F4 to +0x1F8, stores the second argument at +0x210, leaves EAX equal to the copied context+0x1F4 value loaded at 0x00193D6D, and RET 8. Focused seams prove ordered helper calls, exact callback arguments and in-call status; production dependencies remain fatal and the wider service-chain concurrency contract remains open.

PCRTC service helper confirmed by original disassembly. ECX=context; calls 0x00193C40, updates timestamp delta at +0x208/+0x20C, increments +0x1F4, optionally calls 0x00193D10 for occupied slot (1F0&1), spins writing 1 to device+0x600100 while device+0x100 bit 0x01000000 is set, stdcall KeSetEvent(context+0x1C8, 1, FALSE) through IAT 0x001C4014, cdecl-calls context+0x1C4 with {1F4,1F0,reason} or skips if null, restores device+0x6013D4, returns EAX=0, RET. Production KeSetEvent remains the in-place Type-0 dispatcher contract; focused tests seam the IAT and callback.

PGRAPH context-switch service confirmed by original disassembly. ECX=context; FIFO 0x400720=0; when INTR bit 0x1000 set, W1C that bit, spin while 0x400700 nonzero, stdcall 0x00197AAC(channel from trapped_addr>>20). FIFO restored to 1 on the normal exit. NSOURCE/method-0x100 path calls unresolved 0x00193F70; the remaining error combination is INT3. RET, no stack arguments.

Self-contained context tag increment helper called by 0x00196967. Reads one stack argument, increments context+0x19C by that value with x86 32-bit wrap, returns the prior dword in EAX, and RET 4 at 0x00194530. Preserves nonvolatile registers.

Identity-ramp helper called by GPU setup. ECX=context, one stack argument at [esp+4], computes context+0x214+(arg*3*0x100), writes byte values 0..255 to each of three contiguous 256-byte ramps, preserves EBX/ESI/EDI, and returns with RET 4 at 0x00194570.

A vtable method: reached as an indirect call target from 0x0019EE1F (`call dword ptr [eax+4]`, probed at runtime as 0x0019E3B7). The guest body is a complete 13-byte function ending `ret 4` at 0x0019E3C1, and 0x0019E3C4 starts a different function. The DB has no entry here, so the translation pass folded this address into sub_0019E3C4 and the dispatch tuple read `{ 0x0019E3B7u, sub_0019E3C4 }` -- a virtual call therefore entered the wrong body. Recovered so the address keeps its own body and dispatch entry. Third instance of the 0x00168480 class; note the two functions' ESP deltas coincide (both ret 4), so the exact-delta check cannot detect this one -- only entering the wrong code does. Found while attributing a +4 ESP error in logs/runs/20260921-231106-878-esp-window/.

Entered from data: the address is an aligned dword in a .rdata vtable, so it is a function entry by definition. The translation pass classified it tail_jump_alias and folded it into the next entry under the ff4d442 abutting-alias rule -- this entry's end equals that entry's start -- which deleted the body and pointed the dispatch tuple at the wrong function, so a virtual call through the slot executes an unrelated body. The body is a complete function that terminates before the fold target, so the original never fell through into it. Found by scripts/scan-alias-redirects.py, which lists every redirect in this shape. Here: slot 1 of the vtable at 0x001E0DC0 and slot 1 of 0x001E0DE8, so the fold sent AddRef to the unrelated body at 0x0019E613. Measured consequence (logs/runs/20260922-085020-240-trace-ee1f): the ICALL inside 0x0019EE1F -- `if (obj) return obj->vtable[1](obj)` -- ran that body, whose cleanup does not match a RET 4 callee, so 0x0019EE1F returned with the simulated ESP 4 bytes low; its POP ESI then read the pushed argument instead of the saved ESI, and the clobbered ESI made 0x0019F926 write the derived vtable into 0x010DD004 instead of 0x803E4224 and return 0x010DD004. 0x001A0B2B passed that object to 0x001A0A43 as the buffer descriptor, 0x001A09DE read [0x010DD004+0xC] -- the 0x778-byte sound object -- as lpwfxFormat, 0x001A4BC4 matched no format tag and wrote nothing, the device format stayed zero, and 0x001A2BFC divided by it. The real descriptor is the caller's stack struct at [EBP-0x20] in 0x001A0C06, whose +0xC is 0x001A77F0, a valid 48 kHz 16-bit PCM WAVEFORMATEX. Body 0x0019E5CC..0x0019E613 ends RET 4. Evidence: report-deepseek.md, 2026-09-22.
